issue.title: map_to(): missing values outside nonzero map support contaminate valid targets
issue.body:
Reproduced in a fresh R 4.5.1 process against a fresh native build of fmrigds 0.1.0.9000 at commit `273b029bbe9c6c9024bfc12fe4ff6cdb98e18639`. Relevant current GitHub default-branch implementation was also inspected; this report does not claim a full default-branch binary rebuild. Existing open/closed repository issues were searched before filing.

## Reproduction

```r
library(fmrigds)
g <- new_gds(
  list(beta = array(c(2, NA_real_), c(2,1,1)), var = array(1, c(2,1,1))),
  space_sample_labels(c("kept","unused")), "s1", "c1")
out <- compute(map_to(g, space_sample_labels("target"), matrix(c(1,0),1)))
print(as.numeric(assay(out, "beta"))) # NA, expected 2
stopifnot(is.na(assay(out, "beta")[1]))
```

## Expected behavior and scope

A zero map coefficient means that source feature is outside the target's support. Its missing value should not invalidate an otherwise observed target. The independent-variance path uses dense matrix multiplication, so `0 * NA` contaminates the result. This is distinct from missing subjects in a reducer (issue #7). Suggested priority: P2. Iterate nonzero support; preserve missingness for genuinely contributing sources. Do not replace all missing values with zero. A narrow workaround is to subset to the map's actual support before mapping. Regression tests should cover dense/sparse maps, missing effects and variances outside support, and missing values inside support.

issue.title: assert_compatible_spaces() accepts voxel grids with different affines by default
issue.body:
Reproduced in a fresh R 4.5.1 process against a fresh native build of fmrigds 0.1.0.9000 at commit `273b029bbe9c6c9024bfc12fe4ff6cdb98e18639`. Relevant current GitHub default-branch implementation was also inspected; this report does not claim a full default-branch binary rebuild. Existing open/closed repository issues were searched before filing.

## Reproduction

```r
library(fmrigds)
a <- diag(4)
b <- a
b[1,4] <- 10
s1 <- space_voxel(c(2,2,2), a, storage="dense")
s2 <- space_voxel(c(2,2,2), b, storage="dense")
print(assert_compatible_spaces(s1,s2)) # TRUE despite different coordinates
stopifnot(assert_compatible_spaces(s1,s2))
```

## Expected behavior and scope

The default validator checks dimensions and optional identity metadata but omits the voxel affine. Thus equal indices can denote different physical locations while compatibility succeeds. Expected: default voxel-grid compatibility rejects this translation, or an explicitly weaker metadata-only API is clearly distinguished from geometric compatibility. Suggested priority: P2. This is a validator gap, not the NIfTI export affine defects in #6/#8. Workaround: explicitly compare affine and ordered support (or request `fields=c('type','dim','affine')` for this dense example). Passing geometric checks alone still does not establish anatomical registration.

issue.title: harmonise_contrasts() accepts collisions in resulting contrast IDs
issue.body:
Reproduced in a fresh R 4.5.1 process against a fresh native build of fmrigds 0.1.0.9000 at commit `273b029bbe9c6c9024bfc12fe4ff6cdb98e18639`. Relevant current GitHub default-branch implementation was also inspected; this report does not claim a full default-branch binary rebuild. Existing open/closed repository issues were searched before filing.

## Reproduction

```r
library(fmrigds)
g <- new_gds(
 list(beta=array(c(1,2),c(1,1,2)), var=array(1,c(1,1,2))),
 space_sample_labels("f1"), "s1", c("a","b"))
h <- harmonise_contrasts(g,c(a="b"))
print(contrasts(h)) # "b" "b"
print(as.numeric(assay(h,"beta"))) # 1 2: distinct estimates still present
stopifnot(anyDuplicated(contrasts(h)) > 0)
```

## Expected behavior and scope

A partial rename colliding with an unmapped ID produces duplicate contrast identifiers without aggregation or an error. Distinct estimates then have the same lookup key. Expected: validate the entire resulting axis and reject collisions before changing the object. Many-to-one aggregation needs a separate explicit operation and uncertainty rule. Suggested priority: P2. Workaround: validate uniqueness of the full proposed names before calling. Test both mapped-to-mapped and mapped-to-unmapped collisions, and ensure valid renames preserve contrast metadata alignment.

issue.title: Default absolute variance floor changes meta-analysis z and p under unit rescaling
issue.body:
Reproduced in a fresh R 4.5.1 process against a fresh native build of fmrigds 0.1.0.9000 at commit `273b029bbe9c6c9024bfc12fe4ff6cdb98e18639`. Relevant current GitHub default-branch implementation was also inspected; this report does not claim a full default-branch binary rebuild. Existing open/closed repository issues were searched before filing.

## Reproduction

```r
library(fmrigds)
fit <- function(scale=1) {
 g <- new_gds(
  list(beta=array(c(1,2,3)*scale,c(1,3,1)),
       var=array(scale^2,c(1,3,1))),
  space_sample_labels("f1"), c("s1","s2","s3"), "c1")
 compute(reduce(g, method="fixed"))
}
a <- fit()
b <- fit(1e-8)
print(c(original=assay(a,"z_g")[1], rescaled=assay(b,"z_g")[1]))
# 3.464101615, 0.034641016
print(c(original=assay(a,"p_g")[1], rescaled=assay(b,"p_g")[1]))
stopifnot(abs(assay(a,"z_g")[1]-assay(b,"z_g")[1]) > 1)
```

## Expected behavior and scope

Multiplying effects by a positive unit conversion and variances by its square should preserve z and p. The default `eps=1e-12` clamps positive variances below an absolute, unit-dependent floor. Here the original variances are 1 and rescaled variances are 1e-16, all positive and representable; z shrinks by 100. Expected: scale-stable inference, or an explicit regularization policy with units and a visible warning when applied. Suggested priority: P2 (narrow small-variance trigger, but silently changes inference). This is not a request to accept zero/negative variances. A workaround is to express data in units keeping positive variances above the floor; choosing a smaller eps requires care. Tests should cover scale invariance, heterogeneous weights, and invalid variances for both R and compiled paths.
